verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ।
              कथं कुरूणामृषभो हतो भीष्मः शिखण्डिना । कथं रथात् स न्यपतत्पिता मे वासवोपमः ॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said How has that foremost of all the Kurus Bhishma been killed by Shikhandi? How did my sire (Bhishma) who was like a second Indra fall down from his car?

verses.sanskrit: कथमाचक्ष्व मे योधा हीना भीष्मेण सञ्जय । बलिना देवकल्पेन गुर्वर्थे ब्रह्मचारिणा ॥२॥
तस्मिन्हते महाप्राज्ञे महेष्वासे महाबले । महासत्वे नरव्याघ्रे किमु आसीन्मनस्तव ॥३॥
verses.english: On the fall of that foremost of men Bhishma who possessed great wisdom, great ability for action, great powers and great energy what did our warriors thinks in their ininds?

verses.sanskrit: आर्तिं परामाविशति मनः शंससि मे हतम् । कुरूणामृषभं वीरमकम्पं पुरुषर्षभम् ॥४॥
verses.english: Hearing that the foremost of men, the best of the Kurus, the unwavering hero (Bhishma) is killed, my heart is possessed by great grief. sun

verses.sanskrit: के तं यान्तमनुप्राप्ताः के वास्यसन्पुरोगमाः । केऽतिष्ठन्के न्यवर्तन्त केऽन्ववर्तन्त सञ्जय ॥५॥
verses.english: When he advanced who followed him and who went in front? Who stood by his side and who advanced with him?

verses.sanskrit: के शूरा रथशार्दूलमद्भुतं क्षत्रियर्षभम् । तथाऽनीकं गाहमानं सहसा पृष्ठतोऽन्वयुः ॥६॥
verses.english: Who arc those brave warriors that followed that foremost of all car-warriors, that great bowman, that best of the Kshatriya (Bhishma) when he penetrated into the ranks of the enemy?

verses.sanskrit: यस्तमोऽर्क इवापोहन्परसैन्यममित्रहा । सहस्ररश्मिप्रतिमः परेषां भयमादधत् ॥७॥
verses.english: When he attacked the enemy's rank who were the warriors that opposed the chastiser of foes who resembled the and who, spreading terror among the foes destroyed their ranks as the sun destroys darkness, and who achieved exceedingly difficult feats amongst the ranks of the Pandavas?

verses.sanskrit: अकरोद्दुष्करं कर्म रणे पाण्डुसुतेषु यः । ग्रसमानमनीकानि य एनं पर्यवारयन् ॥८॥
कृतिनं तं दुराधर्षं सञ्जयास्य त्वमन्तिके । कथं शान्तनवं युद्धे पाण्डवाः प्रत्यवारयन् ॥९॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, how did the Pandavas oppose in battle that invincible son of Shantanu that accomplished warrior when he attacked them?

verses.sanskrit: निकृन्तन्तमनीकानि शरदंष्ट्रं मनस्विनम् । चापव्यात्ताननं घोरमसिजिह्वं दुरासदम् ॥१०॥
verses.english: How did Kunti's son overthrow in battle that unconquerable one, that fearful bowman scattering fearful arrows, and cutting off the enemies, heads, that invincible hero, modest in every thing, that foremost of all men, stationed on his chariot that hero, having arrows for his teeth, with bow for his wide open mouth, with the terrible sword for his tongue; how was be overthrown, who was never vanquished before and who did not deserve such a fate, that warrior who was as irresistible as the fire of dissolution and seeing whom in battle the great army of the Pandavas were ever filled with terror?
verses.bhavadeepa: अस्य त्वमन्तिके स्थित्वा सर्वं दृष्टवानसीति शेषः ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: अनर्हं पुरुषव्याघ्रं ह्रीमन्तमपराजितम् । पातयामास कौन्तेयः कथं तमजितं युधि ॥११॥
उग्रधन्वानमुग्रेषुं वर्तमानं रथोत्तमे । परेषामुत्तमाङ्गानि प्रचिन्वन्तमथेषुभिः ॥१२॥
पाण्डवानां महत्सैन्यं यं दृष्ट्वोद्यतमाहवे । कालाग्निमिव दुर्धर्षं समचेष्टत नित्यशः ॥१३॥
परिकृष्य स सेनां तु दशरात्रमनीकहा । जगामास्तमिवादित्यः कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम् ॥१४॥
verses.english: Destroying the enemy's troops for ten days that slayer of heroes, having achieved most difficult feats, has now set like the sun.

verses.sanskrit: क्रमेण येन यस्मिंश्च काले यच्च यथाऽभवत् ॥८०॥
verses.english: Destroying the enemy's troops for ten days that slayer of heroes, having achieved most difficult feats, has now set like the sun.

verses.sanskrit: यः स शक्र इवाक्षय्यं वर्षं शरमयं क्षिपन् । जघान युधि योधानामर्बुदं दशभिर्दिनैः ॥१५॥
verses.english: As the result of my evil counsels, that scion of the Bharata race, scattering like Indra himself an inexhaustible shower of arrows, killed in battle one hundred millions of warriors in ten days. He now lies on the bare ground though he deserved it not on the field of battle deprived of life like a great tree uprooted by the wind.

verses.sanskrit: स शेते निहतो भूमौ वातभुग्न इव द्रुमः । मम दुर्मन्त्रितेनाजौ यथा नार्हति भारतः ॥१६॥
कथं शान्तनवं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवानामनीकिनी । प्रहर्तुमशकत्तत्र भीष्मं भीमपराक्रमम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: Seeing the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, of fearful prowess, how could the army of the Panchalas strike him down?

verses.sanskrit: कथं भीष्मेण सङ्ग्रामं प्राकुर्वन्पाण्डुनन्दनाः । कथं च नाजयद्भीष्मो द्रोणे जीवति सञ्जय ॥१८॥
verses.english: How did the Pandavas fight with Bhishma? O Sanjaya, how is it that Bhishma could not conquer when Drona is still alive.

verses.sanskrit: कृपे सन्निहिते तत्र भरद्वाजात्मजे तथा । भीष्मः प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठः कथं स निधनं गतः ॥१९॥
verses.english: When Kripa was near him, when Drona was there, how could Bhishma that foremost of warriors be killed?

verses.sanskrit: कथं चातिरथस्तेन पाञ्चाल्येन शिखण्डिना । भीष्मो विनिहतो युद्धे देवैरपि दुरासदः ॥२०॥
verses.english: How could Bhishma, who was an Atiratha and who could not be resisted even by the celestial be killed in battle by the Panchala Prince Shikhandin?

verses.sanskrit: यः स्पर्धते रणे नित्यं जामदग्न्यं महाबलम् । अजितं जामदग्न्येन शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमम् ॥२१॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, he who always considered himself equal to the mighty son of Jamadagni, he whom Jamadagni's son himself could not conquer, he who resembled Indra in prowess, tell me how such a hero, Bhishma, born as he was in the race of Maharathas, was killed in battle. Without knowing all the particulars, I cannot get rest.

verses.sanskrit: तं हतं समरे भीष्मं महारथकुलोदितम् । सञ्जयाचक्ष्व मे वीरं येन शर्म न विद्महे ॥२२॥
मामकाः के महेष्वासा नाजहुः सञ्जयाच्युतम् । दुर्योधनसमादिष्टाः के वीराः पर्यवारयन् ॥२३॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, (tell me) what great bow men of my army, did not abandon that hero of unfading energy and what brave warriors at the command Duryodhana stood around that hero in order to protect him?

verses.sanskrit: यच्छिखण्डिमुखाः सर्वे पाण्डवा भीष्ममभ्ययुः । कच्चित्ते कुरवः सर्वे नाजहुः सञ्जयाच्युतम् ॥२४॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, when all the Pandavas with Shikhandin at their head advanced against Bhishma, I hope the Kurus stood by the side of the great hero of immeasurable prowess.

verses.sanskrit: अश्मसारमयं नूनं हृदयं मुदृढं मम । यच्छ्रुत्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रं हतं भीष्मं न दीर्यते ॥२५॥
यस्मिन्सत्यं च मेधा च नीतिश्च भरतर्षभे । अप्रमेयाणि दुर्धर्षे कथं स निहतो युधि ॥२६॥
verses.english: There were truth, intelligence and policy to an immeasurable extent in that irresistible chief of the Bharata race. How could he be killed in battle?

verses.sanskrit: मौर्वीघोषस्तनयुत्नुः पृषत्कपृषतो महान् । धनुर्ह्रादमहाशब्दो महामेघ इवोन्नतः ॥२७॥
verses.english: He was like a mighty cloud, the twang of his bow was the roar of that clouds, the arrows were its showers of rains, and the sound of his bow was its thunder. That hero, showering his arrows on the sons of Kunti along with the Panchalas and Srinjayas who were on their side struck down the hostile car-warriors as the slayer of Bala (Indra) struck down the Danavas.

verses.sanskrit: योऽभ्यवर्षत कौन्तेयान्सपाञ्चालान्ससृञ्जयान् । निघ्नन्परथान्वीरो दानवानिव वज्रभृत् ॥२८॥
verses.bhavadeepa: मौर्वीघोषेण स्तनयित्नुर्गर्जन्मेघ इव पृषत्कपृषतो बाणबिन्दुः धनुषैव ह्रादरूपो महाशब्दोऽशनिध्वनिरूपो यस्य ॥२७॥

verses.sanskrit: इष्वस्त्रसागरं घोरं बाणग्रहं दुरासदम् । कार्मुकोर्मिणमक्षय्यमद्वीपं चलमप्लवम् ॥२९॥
verses.english: Who were the heroes that opposed, as the shore resists the surging sea, that chastiser of foes, who was a fearful ocean of arrows and weapons, an ocean in which arrows were the terrible crocodiles, bows were the waves, maces and swords were the sharks, steeds and elephants were the eddies,, the foot soldiers were like so many thousands fishes, and the sounds of conchs and drums its roars, an inexhaustible and agitated ocean without an island and without a raft to cross it, an ocean that swallowed up horses and elephants and foot soldiers by millions, an ocean that drowned all hostile heroes, and that consumed in wrath, the wrath which was its ocean fire?

verses.sanskrit: गदासिमकरावासं हयावर्त्तं गजाकुलम् । पदातिमत्स्यकलिलं शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिःस्वनम् ॥३०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: कार्मुकोर्मिणं चापोर्मिमन्तम् अद्वीपं निराश्रयम् अप्लवं तरणोपायहीनम् ॥२९॥

verses.sanskrit: हयान्गजपदातींश्च रथांश्च तरसा बहून् । निमज्जयन्तं समरे परवीरापहारिणम् ॥३१॥
विदह्यमानं कोपेन तेजसा च परन्तपम् । वेलेव मकरावासं के वीराः पर्यवारयन् ॥३२॥
भीष्मो यदकरोत्कर्म समरे सञ्जयारिहा । दुर्योधनहितार्थाय के तस्यास्य पुरोऽभवन् ॥३३॥
verses.english: Who were in his front when that chastiser of foes Bhishma achieved great feats in battle for the good of Duryodhana?

verses.sanskrit: के रक्षन्दक्षिणं चक्रं भीष्मस्यामिततेजसः । पृष्ठतः के परान्वीरानपासेधन्यतव्रताः ॥३४॥
verses.english: Who were they that protected the right of that immeasurably powerful warrior? Who were they that resisted the enemy's warriors from his rear with patience and energy?

verses.sanskrit: के पुरस्तादवर्तन्त रक्षन्तो भीष्ममन्तिके । के रक्षन्नुत्तरं चक्रं वीरा वीरस्य युध्यतः ॥३५॥
verses.english: Who placed themselves just in front of him to protect him? Who were the heroes that protected the front of that brave warrior when he fought?

verses.sanskrit: वामे चक्रे वर्तमानाः केऽघ्नन्सञ्जय सृञ्जयान् । अग्रतोऽग्र्यमनीकेषु केऽभ्यरक्षन्दुरासदम् ॥३६॥
verses.english: Who were they that placed themselves on his left and attacked the Srinjayas? Who were they that protected the irresistible ranks of his advanced guard?

verses.sanskrit: पार्श्वतः केऽभ्यरक्षन्त गच्छन्तो दुर्गमां गतिम् । समूहे के परान्वीरान्प्रत्ययुध्यन्त सञ्जय ॥३७॥
verses.english: Who protected the wings of that warrior who has gone away to his last journey? O Sanjaya, who were they that fought with the enemy's warriors in general engagement?

verses.sanskrit: रक्ष्यमाणः कथं वीरैर्गोप्यमानाश्च तेन ते । दुर्जयानामनीकानि नाजयंस्तरसा युधि ॥३८॥
verses.english: If he was protected by our warriors and if they protected by him, how is it that he could not defeat in battle the Pandava army, invincible though it was?

verses.sanskrit: सर्वलोकेश्वरस्येव परमेष्ठी प्रजापतेः । कथं प्रहर्तुमपि ते शेकुः सञ्जय पाण्डवाः ॥३९॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, how could the Pandavas succeed in striking Bhishma who was like Parameshti himself, that lord and creator of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्द्वीपे समाश्वस्य युध्यन्ते कुरवः परैः । तं निमग्नं नरव्याघ्रं भीष्मं शंससि सञ्जय ॥४०॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, you tell me of the disappearance of Bhishma, that foremost of men who was our main stay and relying on whom, the Kurus were fighting with their enemies.
verses.bhavadeepa: यः प्रजापतेर्दक्षादेः परमेष्ठी परमे पदे तिष्ठतीति तथा हिरण्यगर्भ इव तस्मिन्निति शेषः ॥३९॥

verses.sanskrit: यस्य वीर्यं समाश्रित्य मम पुत्रो बृहद्बलः । न पाण्डवानगणयत्कथं स निहतः परैः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Alas, how has that greatly powerful warrior, relying on whose prowess my son never cared for the Pandavas, been (today) killed by the enemy?

verses.sanskrit: यः पुरा विबुधैः सर्वैः सहाये युद्धदुर्मदः । काङ्क्षितो दानवान्ध्नद्भिः पिता मम महाव्रतः ॥४२॥
verses.english: In the day of yore when the celestials were fighting with the Danavas, they sought the help of that invincible hero, my great vowobserving father.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्जाते महावीर्ये शान्तनुर्लोकविश्रुतः । शोकं दैन्यं च दुःखं च प्राजहात् पुत्रलक्ष्मणि ॥४३॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, how can you tell me that Bhishma that foremost of all mighty men, that renowned warrior, that great refuge of all, that wise and virtuous man ever devoted to the duties of his order and learned in all the Vedas and their branches, the hero in whose birth Shantanu was freed from all grief, melancholy and sorrow, has been killed?

verses.sanskrit: प्रोक्तं परायणं प्राज्ञं स्वधर्मनिरतं शुचिम् । वेदवेदाङ्गतत्वज्ञं कथं शंससि मे हतम् ॥४४॥
verses.bhavadeepa: पुत्रलक्ष्मणि पुत्रोत्तमे ।  ‘लक्ष्म चिह्ने प्रधाने च’ इति विश्वः ॥४३॥

verses.sanskrit: सर्वास्त्रविनयोपेतं शान्तं दान्तं मनस्विनम् । हतं शान्तनवं श्रुत्वा मन्ये शेषं हतं बलम् ॥४५॥
verses.english: Skilled in every weapon, possessing himself gentleness, and great energy with passions under complete control, hearing that such son of Shantanu (Bhishma) is killed, I consider that rest of my army as already slain.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मादधर्मो बलवान्सम्प्राप्त इति मे मतिः । यत्र वृद्धं गुरुं हत्वा राज्यमिच्छन्ति पाण्डवाः ॥४६॥
verses.english: In my opinion, impiety has now become stronger than piety, for the Pandavas desire sovereignty even killed their venerable Guru.
verses.bhavadeepa: सर्वास्त्रविनयोपेतं सर्वास्त्रशिक्षायुक्तम् । ‘विनया तु बलायां स्त्री शिक्षायां प्रणतौ पुमान्’ इति मेदिनी ॥४५॥

verses.sanskrit: जामदग्न्यः पुरा रामः सर्वास्त्रविदनुत्तमः । अम्बार्थमुद्यतः सङ्ख्ये भीष्मेण युधि निर्जितः ॥४७॥
verses.english: In the days of yore. Rama, the son of Jamadagni, skilled in every weapon and whom none excelled, was vanquished by Bhishma in battle when fighting on behalf of Amba.

verses.sanskrit: तमिन्द्रसमकर्माणं ककुदं सर्वधन्विनाम् । हतं शंससि मे भीष्मं किं नु दुःखमतः परम् ॥४७॥
verses.english: In the days of yore. Rama, the son of Jamadagni, skilled in every weapon and whom none excelled, was vanquished by Bhishma in battle when fighting on behalf of Amba.

verses.sanskrit: असकृत्क्षत्रियव्राताः सङ्ख्ये येन विनिर्जिताः । जामदग्न्येन वीरेण परवीरनिघातिना ॥४९॥
verses.english: That great intelligent one, who was not killed even by that slayer of hostile heroes, that Rama, the son of Jamadagni who defeated in battle all Kshatriyas, has now been killed by Shikhandin,.

verses.sanskrit: न हतो यो महाबुद्धिः स हतोऽद्य शिखण्डिना । तस्मान्नूनं महावीर्याद्भार्गवाद्युद्धदुर्मदात् ॥५०॥
तेजोवीर्यबलैर्यूयान् शिखण्डी द्रुपदात्मजः । यः शूरं कृतिनं युद्धे सर्वशस्त्रविशारदम् ॥५१॥
verses.english: There is no doubt the son of Drupada Shikhandin, who has killed in battle that best of the Bharata race, that hero skilled in the greatest of weapons, that brave and accomplished warrior learned in every weapon, is therefore superior to the invincible and greatly powerful son of Bhrigu (Parashuram) in energy, prowess and might. (Now tell me) who were the warriors that followed the chastiser of focs in that great battle?

verses.sanskrit: परमास्त्रविदं वीरं जघान भग्तर्षभम् । के वीरास्तममित्रघ्नमन्वयुः शस्त्रसंसदि ॥५२॥
शंस मे तद्यथा चासीद्युद्भं भीष्मस्य पाण्डवैः । योषेव हतवीरा मे सेना पुत्रस्य सञ्जय ॥५३॥
verses.english: Tell me how the battle was fought between the Pandavas and Bhishma? O Sanjaya, my army, deprived of its hero, is now like a woman without a protector.

verses.sanskrit: अगोपमिव चोद्भ्रान्तं गोकुलं तद्बलं मम । पौरुषं सर्वलोकस्य परं यस्मिन्महाहवे ॥५४॥
verses.english: That army is now like a panic-stricken herd of kine deprived of its herdsman. When he who possessed prowess superior to that of every man, has fallen in the field of battle, (I guess) what is the mind of my army. O Sanjaya, what power is there in our life.

verses.sanskrit: परासक्ते च वस्तस्मिन्कथमासीन्मनस्तदा । जीवितेऽप्यद्य सामर्थ्यं किमिवास्मासु सञ्जय ॥५५॥
घातयित्वा महावीर्यं पितरं लोकधार्मिकम् । अगाधे सलिले मग्नां नावं दृष्ट्वेव पारगाः ॥५६॥
verses.english: When we have caused our greatly powerful father, that foremost of all virtuous men in the world to be killed? Like a man who, when desirous of crossing the sea, sees the boat sunk down in fathomless water.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मे हते भृशं दुःखान्मन्ये शोचन्ति पुत्रकाः । अद्रिसारमयं नूनं हृदयं मम सञ्जय ॥५७॥
verses.english: I am sure, my sons are bewailing in grief for the death of Bhishma. O Sanjaya, my heart is surely made of stone.

verses.sanskrit: यच्छ्रुत्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रं हतं भीष्मं न दीर्यते । यस्मिन्नस्त्राणि मेधा च नीतिश्च पुरुषर्षभे ॥५८॥
verses.english: For it does not burst even on hearing the death of Bhishma that foremost of all men, in whom were intelligence and policy and skill in arms.

verses.sanskrit: अप्रमेयाणि दुर्धर्षे कथं स निहतो युधि । न चास्त्रेण न शौर्येण तपसा मेधया न च ॥५९॥
verses.english: How has that invincible warrior been killed in battle? Neither by weapons, nor by courage, nor by ascetic merit, nor by intelligence.

verses.sanskrit: न धृत्या न पुनस्त्यागान्मृत्योः कश्चिद्विमुच्यते । कालो नूनं महावीर्यः सर्वलोकदुरत्ययः ॥६०॥
verses.english: Nor by firmness, nor by gift, can a man free himself from death. The greatly powerful Time cannot be transgressed by any thing in the world.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र शान्तनवं भीष्मं हतं शंससि सञ्जय । पुत्रशोकाभिसन्तप्तो महद्दुःखमचिन्तयन् ॥६१॥
verses.english: When, O Sanjaya, as you tell me the son of Shantanu Bhishma is dead. Burning with grief for my sons, nay overwhelmed with great sorrow I hoped for relief from the son of Shantanu, Bhishma. O Sanjaya when he saw Shantanu's son lying dead on the ground like a sun (dropped from the sky) whom did Duryodhana make his refuge? O Sanjaya, reflecting (all I can) with the help of my understanding, I do not see what the end will be of all those kings who are on my side and those who are on the side of the enemy, those that have joined the opposite parties of the battle. Alas, cruel are the Kshatriya duties as fixed by the Rishis, for the Pandavas desire to obtain the sovereignty by even causing the death of Shantanu's son and we too desire to obtain sovereignty by offering that great vowobserving hero as a sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: आशंसेऽहं परं त्राणं भीष्माच्छान्तनुनन्दनात् । यदादित्यमिवापश्यत्पतितं भुवि सञ्जय ॥६२॥
दुर्योधनः शान्तनवं किं तदा प्रत्यपद्मत । नाहं स्वेषां परेषां वा बुद्ध्या सञ्जय चिन्तयन् ॥६३॥
शेषं किञ्चित्प्रपश्यामि प्रत्यनीके महीक्षिताम् । दारुणः क्षत्रधर्मोऽयमृषिभिः सम्प्रदर्शितः ॥६४॥
यत्र शान्तनवं हत्वा राज्यमिच्छन्ति पाण्डवाः । वयं वा राज्यमिच्छामो घातयित्वा महाव्रतम् ॥६५॥
क्षत्रधर्मे स्थिताः पार्था नापराध्यन्ति पुत्रकाः । एतदार्येण कर्तव्यं कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु सञ्जय ॥६६॥
verses.english: The sons of Pritha, as well as my sons are all performing the duties of Kshatriyas. Therefore none of them incurs any sin, O Sanjaya, even a very virtuous man should do it when a great calamity comes.

verses.sanskrit: पराक्रमः पराशक्तिस्तत्तु तस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठितम् । अनीकानि विनिघ्नन्तं ह्रीमन्तमपराजितम् ॥६७॥
verses.english: The display of prowess and the great strength has been considered to be the duty of a Kshatriya. How did the Pandavas oppose my father Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, that invincible but modest hero when he was destroying the troops of the enemy? How were the troops arranged and how did he fight with the illustrious enemies?

verses.sanskrit: कथं शान्तनवं तातं पाण्डुपुत्रा न्यवारयन् ॥ यथायुक्तान्यनीकानि कथं युद्धं महात्मभिः ॥६८॥
कथं वा निहतो भीष्मः पिता सञ्जय मे परैः । दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः ॥६९॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, how was my father Bhishma killed in battle? Duryodhana, Karna and the great skillful Shakuni, the son of Subala.

verses.sanskrit: दुःशासनश्च कितवो हते भीष्मे किमब्रुवन् । यच्छरीरैरुपास्तीर्णां नरवारणवाजिनाम् ॥७०॥
verses.english: And the wily Dushasana, what did they say when Bhishma was killed? Entering that fearful abode of destructive battles play in which the balls have been made by the men, elephants and horses, in which arrows and javelins and swords and darts have formed the dice, who were those notched gamblers that gamble, by taking their very lives who won, who lost who cast the dice with success and who else have been killed besides the son of Shantanu, Bhishma. Tell me all, O Sanjaya, for hearing that Devavrata (of his men) that father of mine, that hero of fearful deeds, that ornament of battle, Bhishma is killed, peace cannot come to me. Thinking that all my sons would be killed, I am affected with the greatest anguish.

verses.sanskrit: शरशक्तिमहाखङ्गतोमराक्षां महाभयाम् । प्राविशन्कितवा मन्दाः सभां युद्धदुरासदाम् ॥७१॥
प्राणद्यूते प्रतिभये केऽदीव्यन्त नरर्षभाः । के जीयन्ते जितास्तत्र कृतलक्ष्या निपातिताः ॥७२॥
अन्ये भीष्माच्छान्तनवात्तन्ममाचक्ष्व सञ्जय । न हि मे शान्तिरस्तीह श्रुत्वा देवव्रतं हतम् ॥७३॥
पितरं भीमकर्माणं भीष्ममाहवशोभिनम् ॥ आर्तिं मे हृदये रूढां महतीं पुत्रहानिजाम् ॥७४॥
त्वं हि मे सर्पिषेवाग्निमुद्दीपयसि सञ्जय । महान्तं भारमुद्यम्य विश्रुतं सार्वलौकिकम् ॥७५॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, you make my that grief blaze forth as fire with Ghee. Sceing Bhishma, celebrated in all the worlds, who undertook a great task, killed, I am sure my sons are lamenting. I desire to hear all their sorrows that have been produced by Duryodhana's act.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा विनिहतं भीष्मं मन्ये शोचन्ति पुत्रकाः । श्रोष्यामि तानि दुःखानि दुर्योधनकृतान्यहम् ॥७६॥
तस्मान्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व यद्वृत्तं तत्र सञ्जय । यद्वृत्तं तत्र सङ्ग्रामे मन्दस्याबुद्धिसम्भवम् ॥७७॥
verses.english: Therefore, O Sanjaya, tell me all that had happened in the battle, the result of my wicked son's folly.

verses.sanskrit: अपनीतं सुनीतं यत्तन्ममाचक्ष्व सञ्जय । यत्कृतं तत्र सङ्ग्रामे भीष्मेण जयमिच्छता ॥७८॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, ill or well, tell me every thing. Tell me all in full and in detail, all that was achieved in the battle of Bhishma ever desirous of victory, by that great warrior skilled in all weapons. How did the battle take place between the armies of the Kurus and the Pandavas and in what manner was the battle fought?

verses.sanskrit: तेजोयुक्तं कृतास्त्रेण शंस तच्चाप्यशेषतः । यथा तदभवद्युद्धं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः ॥७९॥
